column3: [low, intense] In five billion years, the Sun will swallow the Earth.
And you'll still be standing here.
[slow, serious] So how long is forever?
It starts on a Tuesday. Your fourteenth birthday.
Ow, ow, OW!
Rule one. You can still get hurt.
Rule two. You always heal. Every single time.
…huh.
Rule three. You never, ever get older.
[dry] Sounds amazing, right? One more thing. You'll still feel everything.
Because forever is a very, very long time to feel things.
[slowly] Remember that.
Twenty minutes after you wake up, you get the first real test.
[excited] Get it! Get it!
[dazed] …ow?
[panicked] Don't. Move.
A three-meter fall onto concrete. You should be in hospital. Instead…
[excited] Do it again!
That afternoon, the whole family squeezes around the kitchen table. Fourteen candles. One wish.
Fourteen already. You'll be grown before we know it.
This was my father's.
[warmly] Time is the one thing nobody gets more of.
Nobody.
Except you. And at fourteen… you haven't figured out what that means yet.
Of course, nobody believes you. So your best friend wants proof.
[smirking] If you're lying, this is gonna hurt.
Do it again, I wasn't recording.
You can't die. But you can definitely suffer.
[deadpan] …I'm gonna need a form for this.
This part is real. Your cells can only copy themselves about fifty times. Then they stop.
Scientists call it the Hayflick limit. It's the reason everybody gets old.
Everybody… except you.
A week later, Mom drives you to the lab. She hasn't slept since the fall.
Meet the only other one like you.
Here's the crazy part. The Turritopsis jellyfish can turn itself young again. Over and over.
It's the closest thing to immortal that scientists have ever found. Until you.
[softly] You'll outlive everyone you know.
…and doctors say he hasn't aged a single day.
The whole world wants to know how long you'll live. Nobody asks the real question.
How long will they?
Six years later, your best friend is twenty.
Want a ride? Oh wait. You're fourteen. Forever.
Your whole class goes out to celebrate. You go too. For about four seconds.
Nice try, kid.
You will never, ever get in.
License, kid?
I'm thirty-two!
On every photo, you look more and more like somebody's little brother.
Your best friend gets married. You're the best man. Everyone thinks you're the ring boy.
Aren't you adorable!
And for the first time, you notice it. Mom gets tired faster than you do.
Twenty-five years. For them, that's half a life. For you, it's a long weekend.
Opa was right. Nobody gets more time.
Nobody… except you.
So you do the one thing only you can do.
Hey! Kid!
Being unkillable turns out to be very useful.
How old are you?
It's complicated.
Scientists actually measured this.
A falling human reaches about two hundred kilometers an hour.
You feel every single bone.
Okay. No more planes.
Mom and Dad are gone now.
Look at you. Still my little brother.
[warmly] I'm older than you.
Not where it counts.
Sixty years ago, he wanted you to get his football off the roof.
He kept it for sixty years. Just for you.
Don't forget us, okay?
Never.
That's a promise you can't keep. You just don't know it yet.
In 2110, one more visitor makes it up the hill. The last one.
I pushed you off that ramp.
Like a hundred times.
I'm sorry, kid. For all of it.
Here's the hard part. The oldest person who ever lived…
…made it to one hundred and twenty-two.
Somebody's gotta watch your back.
Everyone who ever knew you as a kid… is gone.
And you're still fourteen.
By 2200, a company called EVERGREEN has a plan.
Forever is a product. You're the factory.
They want your cells. Every day. Forever. So the richest people on Earth never die.
So you do what any fourteen-year-old would do.
You're fast. They're faster. And they've got two hundred floors of security.
This is gonna hurt.
You'll still feel everything. But nobody can keep you.
A thousand years. Year three thousand and twenty-six.
And then, one quiet morning, the ground starts to shake.
Buried. No way out.
Remember? You still feel everything.
So you count. One tick at a time.
[whispers] Mom. Dad. Opa. Oma…
Names. Faces. Birthdays. Anything to stay you.
Forty years.
Until one day, somebody finally digs.
Do it again, I wasn't recording.
A thousand years later… kids are exactly the same.
Ten thousand years. Nobody speaks your language anymore.
To them, you're basically a dinosaur.
So you're the only person on the planet who remembers what a Tuesday was.
And this is where physics gets you.
Earth's orbit wobbles in long, slow cycles. And every hundred thousand years or so, the ice comes back.
Your city is down there. Under a kilometer of it.
You can't freeze to death. But you can be cold for ten thousand years.
Here's what nobody warns you about. After fifty thousand years… you can't remember your mom's face.
Only the photo can.
A million years. Humans are leaving Earth for good.
You ask for a seat. Just one.
Every seat is for someone with a lifetime. You have… all of them.
So you're just leaving me here?
Three hundred thousand years of human history. And they leave it with you.
Now you're the only human on Earth.
So you sit down, and you fix the only thing you have left.
Tick.
This part is real. In about two hundred and fifty million years…
…all the continents crash back together into one giant supercontinent.
You walk from what used to be Europe…
…to what used to be America.
Took me six hundred years.
Every year, the Moon drifts about four centimeters away from Earth.
So one day, it's too small to cover the Sun anymore.
You're watching the last total eclipse there will ever be. And nobody else will ever know.
Every billion years, the Sun gets about ten percent brighter.
So the oceans boil away.
The last puddle on Earth takes three seconds to disappear.
Somewhere under here are the oceans you swam in. They're just… gone.
No plants. No animals. No bacteria. You are the last living thing on Earth.
And the clock is still ticking.
Scientists think the Sun will swell up to two hundred times its size.
And it might swallow the Earth whole.
This is where you started this video.
There's no air out here. You can't breathe. And you still… can't… die.
You'll still feel everything. Remember?
Here's the strangest part.
First, the galaxies drift so far apart you can't see them anymore.
In about a hundred trillion years, the last stars in the universe burn out.
[slowly] Then the last one.
Then, very slowly, even the black holes evaporate.
[slow, grave] One googol years. A one... with a hundred zeros.
No stars. No planets. No light. No one.
Just you. Forever.
[serious, clear, full voice] There's no air out here. Sound can't travel through empty space.
So you shouldn't be able to hear that.
But you do.
Something else made it to the end of everything.
[slow, intense] After a googol years... you are not alone.
So… would you take it? Living forever, if this is how it ends?
And who… or what… do you think is out there? Tell me in the comments.
And hit subscribe. You've got time.
